column2: Inspect both cells physically: the wrapping plastic is not torn, dented or swollen. Never use a damaged cell.
Multimeter to V⎓ 20. Measure cell 1: red probe to the + end (the one that sticks out), black to the − end (flat). Write it down.
Measure cell 2 the same way. Write it down.
If the two numbers differ by more than 0.1 V, first charge both cells fully in the iMFG charger (see how to charge), then measure again.

All wire lengths in this part were calculated from the final position of the items in the robot (the layout and the wire table in Part 6), so cut straight to the length written. The numbers already include 3 cm for stripping and slack. Strip 5 mm for ends that are soldered, 11 mm for ends that go into a WAGO.

Before soldering, test first: multimeter in continuity mode. Touch the probes to the 8.4V pad and the ⊕ pad: it must beep. Touch the 0V pad and ⊖: it must not beep. A different result? Stop and photograph both sides of the BMS.
The 8.4V and 0V pads are not soldered yet: they get the holders' own wires in Stage 3.

Cut a red 26 AWG wire 10 cm (no. 4). Slide yellow 2 mm heat shrink on at both ends as the mark of the 4.2V wire, so it is not confused with the red 22 AWG wires. Solder to the 4.2V pad (later to the midpoint).
Cut black 22 AWG 16 cm (no. 8). Solder to the ⊖ pad (− output). Label it "P−". The other end goes into WAGO − in Stage 4.
Leave the ⊕ pad (+ output) for now: its wire comes from the fuse holder in Stage 4.
Wide pads need heat for longer. Apply flux, hold the iron until the solder melts evenly, but no more than about 4 seconds per pad so the MOSFET beside it does not overheat.

First lay things out as they will sit on level 2, so the cut wires fit. Left and right in this guide are seen from behind the robot, facing forward. Holder 1 is at the very back, the spring (−) end on the left. Holder 2 in front of it is flipped: the spring (−) end on the right. The BMS is in front of holder 2, with the 8.4V and 0V pads on the left side (see level 2 in the Part 6 layout drawing).

The holders' own wires are used as they are, not removed from the holders. The black wire of holder 1 is cut to 10 cm (no. 3) from the holder body (to the 0V pad), the red wire of holder 2 to 7 cm (no. 2) (to the 8.4V pad). Strip 5 mm. If the supplied wire is too short, extend it with 22 AWG of the same color.

The midpoint (wire 1): the red wire of holder 1 and the black wire of holder 2 are on the right side. Cut both so that when their ends meet, the total length is about 6 cm (roughly 3 cm from each holder). Strip 5 mm, slide on 4 mm heat shrink, then twist and solder those two ends together with the 4.2V wire (marked yellow). Slide the heat shrink over the joint and heat it. The holders' own wires are thinner than 22 AWG, but since it is only about 6 cm, the heat and voltage lost are very small (about 0.02 V at 3 A).

The holders are still empty. Solder to the BMS in this order: 1. the black wire of holder 1 (−, left) to the 0V pad, 2. the midpoint already connected to 4.2V, 3. the red wire of holder 2 (+, left) to the 8.4V pad. The holders' own wires are thinner than 22 AWG, but the total length of all the thin parts is only about 23 cm, so the voltage lost is about 0.1 V at 3 A: still safe.
Put cell 1 in holder 1, then cell 2 in holder 2. Watch the + mark on the holder (the cell's protruding end to the + side, the spring side to −).
Measure: the 0V wire to the midpoint = the voltage of cell 1. The 0V wire to the 8.4V wire = the sum of both cells.
Measure the output: the ⊕ pad (P+) to the P− wire. It must equal the sum of both cells, about 7.4-8.4 V.

Your fuse is 7.5 A (the number is printed on its body). That suits: the robot's current is usually 1-3 A and can briefly reach about 5-6 A if all four motors stall at once, so 7.5 A does not blow in normal use, but blows at once on a short circuit (tens of amps).
Take both cells out of the holders before soldering at the BMS.

Your fuse holder's wire is very thick (about 12-14 AWG; check the writing on the insulation, or measure the copper: 12 AWG is about 2 mm, 14 AWG about 1.6 mm). Thick is safe, but too stiff and too big for the BMS pad and the switch legs. So cut the loop in the middle, then cut each end again so that 3 cm remains from the holder body. Strip 8 mm.

Cut red 22 AWG 6 cm (no. 5) and 4 cm (no. 6). Slide on 6 mm heat shrink first, wind the 22 AWG end around the thick copper, solder until the solder soaks into both, then close the heat shrink. End 1 gets the 6 cm wire, end 2 gets the 4 cm.
Solder the 22 AWG wire from end 1 to the BMS ⊕ (P+) pad. Label it "P+".
Solder the 22 AWG wire from end 2 to one leg of the rocker switch. If the switch has 3 legs, use the middle leg and one end leg (test with continuity: beeps when ON, silent when OFF).
Cut red 22 AWG 16 cm (no. 7), solder to the switch's other leg. This is the battery plus rail. The soldered switch legs are covered with heat shrink.

WAGO: stick red tape on one WAGO (WAGO +) and black on another (WAGO −). How to insert a wire: lift the orange lever, push in the end stripped 11 mm until it stops, close the lever, tug gently to check.
The plus rail wire from the switch → WAGO +. The P− wire from the BMS → WAGO −. The other holes are for the three converters in Stages 5-7.
Put cell 1 and then cell 2 back in. Switch OFF, measure WAGO + to WAGO − (probes into the small test hole beside the lever): about 0 V. Switch ON: 7.4-8.4 V. Switch OFF again.
Switch OFF. Cut red 22 AWG 15 cm (no. 9) and black 15 cm (no. 10). Red: WAGO + → IN+. Black: WAGO − → IN−. Tighten the terminal screws, tug the wires gently to check.
Nothing is on OUT+ / OUT− yet. Switch ON.
Press the button until the OUT LED lights. Also measure OUT+ to OUT− with the multimeter.
Turn the trimpot slowly while watching the multimeter. If the number goes up, turn the other way. Stop at 5.0 V (4.95-5.1 is fine).
Switch OFF then ON again. Measure again: still 5.0 V.
Put a tape label "5V LOGIKA" on this module.
Flip the XL4015 board over and read the IN+, IN−, OUT+, OUT− text under the terminals. Mark them with a marker on top of the board.
Switch OFF. Cut red 22 AWG 26 cm (no. 11) and black 21 cm (no. 12) (longer because the XL4015 will be on level 2, at the front). Red: WAGO + → IN+. Black: WAGO − → IN−. No load on OUT yet.
Switch ON. Measure OUT+ to OUT−.
Turn trimpot 3 a few turns while watching the multimeter. If the voltage changes, that is the voltage trimpot (CV). If it does not change, put it back, then try trimpot 4.
Set the CV trimpot to 6.0 V (5.9-6.1). Never above 6.2 V: TT motors and MG90S servos are designed for 6 V at most.
Do not change the CC trimpot yet. Put the label "6V MOTOR" on the module.

Switch OFF. Prepare two more WAGOs: green tape (WAGO 6V) and black tape marked 6 (WAGO −6). Cut green 22 AWG 15 cm (no. 15): OUT+ → WAGO 6V. Cut black 10 cm (no. 16): OUT− → WAGO −6. Switch ON, measure WAGO 6V to WAGO −6: still 5.9-6.1 V.
Switch OFF. Cut red 22 AWG 16 cm (no. 13) and black 16 cm (no. 14). Red: WAGO + → IN+, black: WAGO − → IN−.
Adjust to 5.0 V with no load, as in steps 2-5 of Stage 5.
Put the label "5V KAMERA" on it.
Switch OFF. On the breadboard, place an LED and a 330 Ω resistor in series: the LED's long leg to one end of the resistor.
Connect the resistor's other end to OUT+ of LM2596 #1, the LED's short leg to OUT−.
Switch ON: the LED lights. Measure OUT again: still about 5.0 V.
Move it to WAGO 6V and WAGO −6 (XL4015): the LED still lights, slightly brighter.
Switch OFF. Remove the LED and resistor.
